name: Horse gram (Kulattha, Dolichos biflorus)
short: Food allergy: a skin-test and IgE study identified 2 of 48 atopic people as allergic to horse gram lectin (first such report). No other human safety data were found.
text: In a study of skin prick tests with horse gram lectin (Dolichos biflorus agglutinin), 10 of 48 atopic people (21%) tested positive and none of 20 non-atopic people did; two of the atopic people had lectin-specific IgE antibodies and were identified as having food allergy to horse gram, which the authors describe as the first report of food allergy to horse gram, identifying the lectin as an allergen. The abstract does not describe what reactions, if any, these two people had after eating horse gram. A review of horse gram lists phytic acid among its non-nutritive bioactive substances, and a separate review of legumes in general (not horse gram specifically) states that phytate is a main inhibitor of iron and zinc absorption from legumes, while noting that in a balanced diet containing animal protein a high intake of legumes is not considered a risk for mineral supply. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
